scope: Native analytic narrow-phase first pass: ball-ball, ball with cuboid/capsule/cone/cylinder in both orders, cuboid-cuboid, materials, parent IDs and inert deferred slots
tolerance_reason: Existing f32 tolerances apply to generated contact coordinates, normals, separation, materials and extents. Only near-axis interior ball/capsule/cone/cylinder contacts permit a different symmetry direction; both outputs must independently satisfy the surface, closest-distance, unit-normal and normal-direction checks. Distance/materials remain tolerance-compared and all integer fields remain exact.
preconditions: Valid flat collider-pair list, global parent IDs, unit finite poses and native Rust-derived layouts
Finite nonnegative primitive dimensions, finite materials and nonnegative prediction distance; zero-length capsules are supported
Analytic-only ContactPlan with pfm_base == bound and pfm_len == 0; deferred slots are cleared but not otherwise generated
invariants: Every pair owns its positional manifold slot; a miss, same-body pair or deferred shape changes only its len to zero
Written collider/body IDs and unused manifold storage remain exact; active point count agrees with Rust
All native material combine rules, stronger-rule priority and unknown-rule Average fallback follow Rust
Box SAT axes, support-face order, clipping candidate order and four-point reduction follow Rust
Axial symmetry is a geometric equivalence exception, not a wider global float tolerance; invalid Rust geometry is rejected too
All input buffers and inactive capacity remain unchanged
outside_scope: Deferred PFM/GJK/EPA, triangle mesh and polyline manifold generation
Contact plan publication, reduction of multiple composite manifolds and sort schedules
Full scene integration, long-run stability and the separate zero-distance Coulomb numerical block
Ascend vendor compilation, execution and performance

numerical_policies.scope: Single-point ball contact on the interior axis of a capsule, cone or cylinder within 32 f32 eps times shape scale
checks: Unchanged pair/parent IDs, len, materials and separation
Finite unit normal and actual closest boundary point for both Rust and TileLang
Contact normal follows the boundary direction, including ball-first frame conversion
